logic.note: Runs the real compiled arduino-esp32 3.3.12 firmware (ESP-IDF 5.5) in Espressif's QEMU 9.2.2 (ESP32-C3 machine) with Jumper's patches (jb7), in Docker or a native build, in lockstep with the circuit. Verified on real firmware: GPIO outputs and inputs with the chip's pull-ups / pull-downs, UART0 (Serial) and UART1, I2C0 (Wire) to the I2C parts, PWM (LEDC / analogWrite), GPIO interrupts (attachInterrupt) and the ADC (analogRead). SPI does not work yet (transfers do not come through), RMT (NeoPixel) is untested, Touch is not emulated. I2S is (jb6: ESP_I2S out and in, verified on real firmware on the ESP32, S3 and C3). docs/boards.md has the per-peripheral status with the test behind each cell.

timing.note: QEMU runs in lockstep with Jumper's virtual clock (-icount, one instruction = 8 ns, -rtc clock=vm), so millis(), delay() and the order of pin events are deterministic and repeat exactly. Instruction timing is not cycle-accurate: code runs at about 125 M instructions per virtual second whatever the real 160 MHz pipeline, caches and flash wait states would do, so tight loops and bit-banged protocols run at a different speed than on the chip.

analog.note: Pins are ideal sources with 30 Ω output resistance (default 20 mA drive) and 45 kΩ internal pull-ups / pull-downs. Digital inputs switch at 0.25 × and 0.75 × VDD and keep their last level in between. analogRead() reads the pad voltage the circuit solved, converted by the emulator's ADC model (not the real chip's non-linearity, attenuation error or noise); LEDC PWM (analogWrite, servos, tone()) is drawn on the pin as edges.

power.note: Round 10: USB (power.usb) is 5 V on the 5V pad; without it the board runs from 5V or the BAT pad through its power path and LDO, the board draws its typical current, and the firmware is held in reset while 3V3 is under 3.0 V. The on-board ETA4054S2F charger charges a cell on BAT from USB at 380 mA (trickle 40 mA below 2.9 V, CV at 4.2 V, done below a tenth of that). Wi-Fi transmit peaks (up to 350 to 500 mA), sleep currents and brown-out behaviour are not simulated.

radio.note: The radio is not emulated (QEMU has no radio model): no RF, signal, range or roaming, and no Bluetooth / BLE. Wi-Fi sketches (WiFi.h, HTTPClient, WebSockets, MQTT) run unchanged in Jumper's simulation build: a Wi-Fi shim carries them over an emulated Ethernet card into Jumper's sandbox network (mocks, cassettes, faults such as wifi_drop and weak_signal); partial on the ESP32-C3 (a WiFi.h + HTTPS sketch ran through it). Test range, real access points and everything Bluetooth on the real board.

emulates: ESP32-C3 (single-core RISC-V) running the real compiled firmware in Espressif's QEMU, in lockstep with the circuit
Digital I/O with the chip's internal pull-ups / pull-downs, 3.3 V thresholds
Serial (UART0) as the console, with virtual time stamps
I2C0 (Wire) to the I2C parts, PWM (LEDC / analogWrite), GPIO interrupts (attachInterrupt), UART1 and the ADC (analogRead), verified on real firmware
On-board Li-ion charger (ETA4054S2F, 380 mA) and the battery power path

Wi-Fi sketches (WiFi.h, HTTPClient, WebSockets, MQTT) run unchanged in Jumper's simulation build: a Wi-Fi shim carries them over an emulated Ethernet card into Jumper's sandbox network (mocks, cassettes, faults such as wifi_drop and weak_signal) (partial on the ESP32-C3 (a WiFi.h + HTTPS sketch ran through it))

I2S audio out and in (ESP_I2S / ESP-IDF i2s_std, i2s_pdm): the DMA paced at the configured sample rate, frames to Jumper's I2S bus (a MAX98357A plays them; a microphone part answers reads); not the BCK / WS pin edges
doesNotEmulate: The radio itself (Wi-Fi RF and Bluetooth / BLE): Wi-Fi sketches run through Jumper's sandbox network instead (docs/network.md); BLE does not work
The SPI peripheral (SPI transfers do not come through yet); RMT (NeoPixel / WS2812) is untested
Deep sleep, light sleep and their currents
Pull-ups / pull-downs the chip applies at reset before the firmware sets them (only the ones the firmware sets are seen)
Reset and boot from the EN / RST and BOOT pins, and the strapping levels themselves (check_design checks them instead)
The second core's timing (both cores run, in one QEMU thread)
The native USB port (USB CDC): in the simulator Serial is UART0
testOnRealDevice: Wi-Fi range, real access points and real servers, and everything Bluetooth
Timing-critical code (bit-banged protocols, tight loops): instruction timing is approximate
Upload with esptool / Arduino IDE (strapping pins at reset)
Every 5 V part: ESP32 pins are not 5 V tolerant; use a level shifter
Battery charging current and the charge LED
